subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module to build a futuristic militarized cyberpunk truck using just the SDK, designing the chassis joint root and wheel joint structure for a 6x6 armored vehicle.

I'm working out the dimensions and skeleton layout -- axle positions, wheel radii, chassis hub heights, and joint hierarchy for the hull, wheels, turret, and hinged doors -- then moving on to planning the surface textures with warning stripes and armor paneling.

For textures I'm planning around six: an emblem decal, hazard stripes, a HUD screen, a stenciled license tag "TX-2077", a glowing neon logo, and a tread pattern, plus using the panelled metal paint from the clockwork kit for the hull and a custom gunmetal paint with dirt wear and countershading for the body, keeping the overall color palette tight.

Now I'm setting up box and cylinder helpers and a paint wrapper function, with bones defaulting to the nearest joint unless I specify the chassis bone. Then I'm laying out the chassis frame with rails, crossmembers, and a lofted skid plate, designing the hull with lofted stations for the lower body and an angular frustum-box cab, placing the cab forward with a sloped wedge hood and the cargo bed toward the rear as an armoured modular box with glowing strips, and considering a turret mounted on the cab roof.

Now I'm placing a remote turret with a railgun on the rear cargo roof, defining the chassis joint and lofted lower hull with a tapered front nose wedge, and building the cab as a sequence of lofted stations that narrow and slope upward into a wedge hood. I'm also planning the angled windscreen as a dark teal glass slab rotated into place.

Defining the lower body tub box dimensions and position explicitly to keep floating issues minimal.

I'm figuring out wheel placement and arches: narrowing tub width so wheels slightly overlap the sides, then adding fender boxes positioned above each wheel to cover the overlap.

Working out the lower tub dimensions and nose taper using a frustum shape so the front narrows smoothly from the main body width down toward the front, keeping cab proportions wider above the wheel line.

Now I'm sketching the cab and hood: a boxy cab section sitting above the tub, a tapered hood frustum narrowing toward the front, and a tilted windscreen slab angled back from the cab front.

Still working out the frustum geometry...

Computing the windscreen's outward-facing normal and offsetting its center accordingly, then sizing it to fit the sloped face length. I'm also working out the side windows, placing thin angled glass boxes near the tapering body sides with a slight rotation to match the greenhouse slope.

Working out the window placement with the tapering width, then adding a roof sensor deck plate and planning the cargo module box dimensions behind the cab, leaving a gap between the sections.

I'm closing that gap with a bridging walkway and planning the cargo module's features: paneling, hazard stripes, glowing vents, a rear ramp hinge, and a roof-mounted turret with yaw/pitch joints, a glowing railgun barrel, and missile pods, plus a light bar and sensor dome on the cab roof, and six wheels with toroidal tires.

For the wheels, I'm designing each with a cylindrical tire, tread blocks, rim, hub, lug nuts, and a glowing neon hub ring, merging the tread and lug geometry per wheel to keep the part count manageable across all six wheels within the overall budget.

Writing geometry transform helpers...

Rim and hub details next: dark cylinder rim, glowing cyan beadlock ring, octagon hub cap, merged lug nuts, skipping brake rotor visibility. Then suspension components—axle rods, leaf springs, shocks, and a spherical differential housing centered between wheels.

Now I'm considering steering joints for the front axle, naming conventions like wheelFL, and setting up a steer joint parented to the chassis with the wheel attached to it, working out hinge directions for the joint sampler.

Now I'm defining the gunmetal body paint material, mixing dark hex colors with noise and dirt gradients based on surface position.

Then I'm applying panel paneling to the hull and working out texel density to pick a paint resolution large enough that 2.5mm panel seams won't disappear—settling on a higher resolution to keep seams visible.

I'll write my own panel-line paint function with wider seams based on fractional cell position, applying it only to major body parts to keep the texture atlas manageable, and plan SVG textures starting with yellow/black hazard stripes for flat surfaces.

Then I'm sketching more texture ideas: a unit emblem/insignia for cargo sides, stenciled "UNIT-77 // RAZOR" text, a glowing HUD-style display panel, and a geometric neon glyph in place of risky CJK text rendering, plus a vent detail to round out the set.

I also want a grille texture with teeth-like patterns and an angular cyberpunk "face" look up front using glowing slit headlights — settling on roughly six to seven decal textures total (hazard, emblem, stencil, screen, grille, neon glyph). I'll apply these as plane-geometry decals offset slightly off the surface at the right positions and orientations on each part.

I'm deciding which textures should glow versus stay flat — the hazard and emblem stay matte while the neon glyph uses an emissive map so it lights up, keeping darker regions dark only for the glowing ones. Now I'm drawing up a limited flat color palette of about twenty hues for consistency across the whole model.

For the glass, I'm keeping it a dark teal base and considering a thin translucent decal of reflection streaks layered just in front, using an alpha-cutout texture so only the streak shapes show through.

Now I'm setting up imports from the builder library and its glow kit, plus a geometry merge utility, while deciding to define my own degree constant rather than rely on an uncertain export.

Writing helper functions...

Now I'm sketching out the skeleton structure: a chassis joint as the spine, then wheel axles for front/mid/rear with mirrored left/right sides, plus a turret joint parented to the chassis with yaw rotation.

I'm also placing a ramp joint at the rear bottom for a hinged door panel, figuring out its rotation axis so the door hangs flush against the rear face, then starting to add cab door hinge joints at the front edges.

I'm aiming for a compact but detailed script, around 450 lines, and now sketching out the paint functions that blend base metal tones with grime and weathering noise based on surface normals and height.

Writing plated texture function...

Adding per-panel tone variation using a hash-based pseudo-random function, then blending it subtly into the color. I'm also considering hazard-stripe textures, using an SVG pattern with yellow and black diagonal polygons for warning paint.

Designing more texture assets: an emblem with a ring, hexagon, and fang chevron plus "77" text; a stencil reading "RZR-77 // CORP SEC" in bold monospace with an outline; a dark screen texture with cyan graph lines, magenta bars, and glowing "TGT LOCK" text; and a grille texture with steel teeth against a dark background, kept non-glowing.

I'm also sketching a magenta glowing triangle-eye glyph for door decals, considering a "2077" number plate reusing the stencil function with different text, and writing a decal helper that places textured planes onto bones with configurable size, position, direction, and optional glow.

For orientation, I'm working out which way text reads depending on viewing angle -- since a plane facing +X gets viewed by someone standing at +X looking back toward -X, their right-hand side maps to -Z, so I need to account for that when deciding whether text needs mirroring on opposite sides of the truck.

Now I'm setting up the build script structure: defining metadata for the vehicle, creating a builder with a chassis joint as the spine bone, and a helper function for placing parts relative to that bone. I'm also adding a transform helper that composes position, rotation, and scale into a matrix for baking merged geometry.

Writing transform helper...

Now I'm laying out the hull geometry -- frame rails, crossmembers, the tub body, and starting the nose as a tapered frustum shape connecting two cross-sections.

Next I'm adding a skid plate underneath and side armor plates positioned between the front and middle wheel axles.

Working out fender placement above the wheel tops, with a flare lip on the outer edge and a rubber mud flap trailing behind each wheel.

Then I'm positioning the upper cargo module box itself, making sure its bottom edge aligns with the tub top and its rear extends to the correct z-position, before adding bevel detailing to the frame edges.

Still working on cargo details...

Still placing geometry details...

Adjusting the greenhouse frustum and hood dimensions...

I'm adding a center spine ridge box tilted about 10° to match the hood's slope, placed near the top where the hood surface begins to angle downward, then planning three vent slits on the hood.

Positioning side armor skirts and intakes along the hood, then working out the front fascia—placing a grille plane near the nose where the hood and tub meet at the front.

Still building bumper details...

Now adding roof-mounted sensors, radar dish, antennas, and mirror assemblies with camera boxes to the cab.

For the doors, I'm planning panel geometry with handles, glow slits, and decal details, plus armor plating and step boards positioned near the front axle gap.

Now I'm designing the turret assembly on the cargo roof: a bolted base ring, a yaw drum joint with shield and sensor plates, and a pitch joint carrying a railgun breech with twin barrel rails.

Then I'm detailing the railgun coils, capacitor drums, glowing rail gap, missile pods, muzzle brake, and curved ammo belt, followed by underglow strips of magenta and cyan boxes placed along the tub sides.

Now I'm routing coolant pipes and conduit bundles between the cab and cargo using curved sweeps, then positioning vertical exhaust stacks near the cab-cargo seam, working out their exact x and z placement so they clear both body widths.

Underneath the cargo sides I'm hanging fuel and battery tanks between the wheels, adding glow strips to the battery boxes. For paint, I'm planning distinct hull materials for cab versus cargo, with a cyberpunk palette of gunmetal body panels accented by magenta, cyan, and hazard yellow stripes.

I'm also sketching a cheap digital camo effect using noise-threshold blending into a dark steel tone, then checking the sweep/rod/spike/frustumBox/lathe API signatures before writing the wheel function.

Writing wheel function code...

Still adding tire details...

Still adding wheel details and joints...

Adding shock absorbers and spring coils...

Working out the drive shaft placement and rotation parameters for each part, then moving on to generating the hazard stripe SVG pattern...

Still writing SVG code...

Still sketching icon variants...

I'm settling on roughly eight textures total, combining the stencil variants with distinct text labels, then moving to write the actual module code, keeping the texture definitions organized at the top and deciding where to place the glyph decals on the vehicle body—favoring the doors and tail rather than the roof.

Now I'm laying out the roof turret assembly: the pitch joint position, the breech box, the parallel rails, and a glowing cyan gap running between them to give the gun a lit seam effect.

Still placing weapon geometry...

Adding more cab details...

Adding rear corner spikes with glowing red tips, then thinking through the mirrors as angled rods with dark glass boxes and small orange turn signal glow strips mounted on each side.

Working out the cab door geometry now, placing the hinge, panel, handle, and a glowing neon side marker decal on the door bone.

Then I'm counting up all the decal calls across the vehicle—cargo emblems, stencils, screen, grille vents, hazard strips, rear plate—to keep track of total decoration budget. I'm also figuring out where to tuck fuel tanks and batteries in the gaps between wheels, considering floor clearance under the cargo tub.

Now I'm placing cylindrical fuel tanks rotated to lie along the frame axis, positioning them so they clear the wheel radius zone and sit beside the rails without overlapping the tub. I'm adding torus-shaped straps around each tank using their default axis orientation to visually secure them in place, plus some coolant piping details.

I'll use a seeded random generator to scatter rivets, grime, and small greebled boxes across the cargo roof for visual texture, keeping variable usage minimal to avoid any strictness issues. Starting to write the final TypeScript file now, importing the geometry merge utility...

Still writing imports and camo paint function...

Adding cab base paint and rivet helpers...

Confirmed, rotating 90 degrees about X sends the cone's axis to point along +z. Now I'll pull everything together into the final code.
